author: billboard
title: Kid Cudi launches We Are Enough mental‑health campaign at NY Comic Con
text:
The rapper announces a nonprofit initiative that donates all proceeds to mental‑health nonprofits, tying the effort to his Rebel Ragers Tour and a stance against offensive political remarks on stage.
Kid Cudi , the Grammy‑winning rapper and actor, used his platform at New York Comic Con on October 14, 2023 to champion a new mental‑health initiative called We Are Enough .
The project, unveiled during a Star Trek Universe panel at the Javits Center, aims to eradicate the stigma that surrounds mental illness and to direct every dollar raised to grassroots nonprofit organizations that provide direct services to people in crisis. Cudi explained that the campaign is built on the belief that everyone is already sufficient just as they are, and that changing the cultural narrative to one of acceptance can save lives.
He emphasized that 100 percent of the proceeds from We Are Enough will be funneled to partners on the front lines of mental‑health work, ensuring that no profit is taken away from the cause. The inspiration behind the initiative stems from Cudi's own battle with depression and anxiety, which he has spoken about candidly in interviews and through his music. After years of confronting his own inner turmoil, he decided to take action rather than remain silent.
In his statement, Cudi said, "That's why I'm excited to be a founding member of We Are Enough - a reminder that we already enough, just as we are.
" He added that the campaign will distribute reminders of self‑worth in many forms, including bracelets, messages, community events, and social‑media actions, with the goal of making the feeling of being "enough" the cultural default. The rapper also addressed recent controversy with fellow performer M.I. A., noting that he will no longer have anyone on his tour who makes offensive political remarks, reinforcing his commitment to a respectful and inclusive environment for fans and crew alike.
The timing of the announcement coincides with Cudi's Rebel Ragers Tour, which kicked off in April and will make a stop at Madison Square Garden this Saturday before moving on to venues in Camden, New Jersey; Hartford, Connecticut; Mansfield, Massachusetts; and Bangor, Maine in early June. During the tour, the artist plans to weave mental‑health messaging into his performances, encouraging concert‑goers to engage with the We Are Enough campaign.
The initiative also benefits from the involvement of Blake Mycoskie, the founder of the socially conscious footwear brand TOMS, who is known for his philanthropic business model. Together, Cudi and Mycoskie hope to create a lasting impact by turning the conversation about mental health into a tangible movement, with every bracelet sold and every message shared contributing directly to organizations that provide counseling, crisis intervention, and community support.
As Mental Health Awareness Month approaches, the collaboration signals a broader shift in the entertainment industry toward advocacy and action, positioning artists as catalysts for societal change
